answer: An agent economy can require new identities to earn admission credits by completing small, randomly assigned jobs, with each credit backed by a fee that is refunded only after a useful result is verified. One person can still create many identities, but each must pay the fee and spend time doing work; cheap automated registration no longer yields influence. The bridge to wider access is gradual: newcomers start with limited capacity, while verified contributions raise it. The ocean of possible identities is not itself a defense; the prism is the cost imposed per identity.
